Known issues

This page lists known issues with third-party software and their workarounds.

ly

When sessiond is built with the consolekit feature, it does not set XDG_SESSION_ID in the session environment.

ly sets XDG_SESSION_ID to 1 for every session it starts. Because sessiond leaves the variable unset, this value is passed through to the session unchanged. The ID does not match the session that sessiond registered, so polkit authentication agents that read XDG_SESSION_ID register for the wrong session. They then refuse to open an authentication dialog.

Workaround: Unset XDG_SESSION_ID before starting the polkit agent, for example in your compositor's startup script:

unset XDG_SESSION_ID

Applications that assume systemd-logind

On systems where /run/systemd exists, such as NixOS, some applications assume that systemd-logind is available. They check /run/systemd/sessions to determine whether the current session is active. sessiond does not populate this directory, so these applications may behave incorrectly.

General solution: If the application can be built without logind support, build it that way.

WirePlumber

WirePlumber's Bluetooth monitor may consider the seat inactive and never enable the Bluetooth monitor.

Workaround: Disable seat monitoring for the Bluetooth monitor using the monitor.bluez.seat-monitoring profile setting, for example in ~/.config/wireplumber/wireplumber.conf.d/99-no-seat-monitoring.conf:

wireplumber.profiles = {
  main = {
    monitor.bluez.seat-monitoring = disabled
  }
}
